Matrix view for ctStanModel objects

Source: R/ctStanModel.R
ctModelMatrices.Rd

Access or replace the matrix representation of a ctStanModel while keeping the pars data frame as the canonical model specification.

Usage

ctModelMatrices(x)

ctModelMatrices(x) <- value

Arguments

x

A ctStanModel object.

value

A named list of matrices, typically copied from ctModelMatrices(x) or x$matrices.

Value

ctModelMatrices() returns a named list of matrices. The replacement form returns the updated ctStanModel.

Details

ctModelMatrices(x) reconstructs matrices from x$pars. The replacement form updates matching matrix, row, and col entries in x$pars. Numeric matrix entries become fixed values; non-numeric entries become parameter labels. Metadata such as transforms and individual variation settings is preserved when possible and reset to fit-ready defaults when fixed/free status changes.

The same view is available as x$matrices. Direct replacements such as x$matrices$DRIFT[1, 2] <- "cross" update x$pars; detached copies must be assigned back with x$matrices <- mats. A placeholder matrices element is stored in the object so the view is visible in names(x) and printed objects, but the matrix values are always derived from x$pars.

The view also holds the population spread of the individually varying parameters: RAWPOPVAR for the subject level and RAWPOPVAR_<idname> for each grouping level, one row and column per parameter varying at that level, also reachable as x$RAWPOPVAR. The diagonal holds standard deviations, and the lower triangle values that determine the correlations, both for the raw, untransformed parameters, the scale a fit reports them on. A number fixes a cell, and a label leaves it free. ctCov writes a whole matrix from a covariance matrix, and can also be used to give T0VAR, DIFFUSION or MANIFESTVAR as a covariance matrix.

Examples

model <- ctModel(LAMBDA = diag(2), manifestNames = c('Y1', 'Y2'),
  latentNames = c('eta1', 'eta2'))

# The model as matrices. A label is a free parameter and a number a fixed
# value. DRIFT[1, 2] is the effect of eta2 on eta1.
mats <- ctModelMatrices(model)
mats$DRIFT

# Fix the effect of eta2 on eta1 to zero, and give both auto effects the
# same label so that they are estimated as one parameter.
mats$DRIFT[1, 2] <- 0
mats$DRIFT[2, 2] <- 'drift_eta1'
ctModelMatrices(model) <- mats
model$pars[model$pars$matrix == 'DRIFT', c('row', 'col', 'param', 'value')]

# A single cell can be changed through model$matrices.
model$matrices$DRIFT[1, 2] <- 'drift_eta1_eta2'

# The spread over subjects of the individually varying parameters, here
# the initial means and the manifest means. Standard deviations are on
# the diagonal and correlation parameters below it.
model$RAWPOPVAR
